summary: This standards-track memo adds new public key algorithms to the Secure Shell protocol so RSA keys can be used with SHA-256 and SHA-512 for server and client authentication. It updates RFC 4252 and RFC 4253. This lets SSH keep using existing RSA keys while moving away from the older SHA-1 hash.

eli5.summary: Your old key still fits the lock, but now the lock checks it with a stronger stamp. SSH can use the same RSA keys with a better fingerprint method.

questions: how to use rsa keys with sha-256 in ssh
